text: 🇲🇽🏛️ 17,000 archaeological pieces returned to Mexico since 2018, ten times more than under previous governments. — Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture In the last two years alone, 5,686 pieces were restituted with the Foreign Ministry, "a reflection of a different vocation and commitment to our memory and heritage." Another 520 million pesos went to the conservation of 74 archaeological zones and 34 museums.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It cannot be that cases of child abuse come out on social media, and that the networks do nothing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 2, 2026 On Oct 1, two adult brothers, both former students, entered Secondary School No. 13 in Torreón, Coahuila, and attacked staff and students with knives. A member of the school's leadership was killed and four people were injured. Investigators found similarities with a recent case in Querétaro and two or three others involving communication over social media. Sheinbaum formed a working group led by Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde, with experts from UNAM and IPN. The goal is a decree next week obliging platforms to take down content that incites violence and report it, defined clearly "so they don't border on censorship."

🇲🇽🕊️ "Never again, never again a repression by the State against a social movement." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 2, 2026 Today marks 58 years since the October 2, 1968 massacre of students in the Plaza de Tlatelolco. Sheinbaum opened the mañanera with "October 2 is not forgotten" and recalled that two years ago, on taking office, her government published a statement in the Official Gazette naming then-president Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, commander of the armed forces, as the main person responsible, as he himself acknowledged after leaving office.

🇲🇽🎻 "For those of us who study the arts, this gesture means that our vocation matters." — Gracia Shalom López Martínez, 16, CEDART arts high school student Students from the renovated public art schools closed the mañanera. "Every peso invested here will multiply into creativity, discipline and pride for our country," López said. Lara García, a full-time student at INBAL's National School of Folkloric Dance, said the renovation "has dignified our profession." Musicians from the Carlos Chávez Orchestra School said that in May, after years "in a hotel, in a borrowed place," they finally got a school of their own.

🇲🇽📚 Zero VAT for bookstores, and dubbing actors' voices protected from AI. — Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture The 2027 budget proposal includes a zero rate for bookstores, "a historic demand," worth 200 million pesos a year to the book ecosystem. A reform to the Federal Labor Law and the Copyright Law now expressly protects dubbing artists, performers and interpreters against misuse of their voices or their alteration with artificial intelligence. More than 2,600 Culture Ministry workers, who had the lowest salaries in the federal government, were regraded for the first time in 10 years, a 17% raise. One million free copies of a new collection of Mexican women authors will be given away at year's end.
banner: BOOKS: 0% VAT · VOICES SAFE FROM AI

text: 🇲🇽🎨 Public art schools: 1.85 billion pesos, an investment without precedent in 40 years, and no more enrollment fees. — Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture In two years, 2,352 spaces were renovated in the schools of INBAL, INAH, the Film Training Center and the Carlos Chávez Orchestra School, which now has its own building after 37 years. Enrollment fees were eliminated "to guarantee free artistic education." Support for artists rose 45%, from 1,840 to 2,658 million pesos, reaching more than 180,000 artists. Cultural programming grew 32%: 520,000 activities in all 32 states, with 50 million attendees.
banner: ART SCHOOLS: BIGGEST REBUILD IN 40 YEARS

text: 🇲🇽📱 "The platforms have to prove to us that they are safe places for minors." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education "With all the artificial intelligence they have, of course they are capable of detecting in time and removing content that incites violence." Delgado noted that similar steps are being taken in other countries, including the United States. Sheinbaum said Meta's settlement in the big US trial includes getting rid of likes, limiting minors to a couple of hours a day and shutting the platform off at night: "That shows that greater responsibility is possible." Schools are also reinforcing the "ABC of Emotions" program, with parent assemblies, confidential mailboxes and the Línea de la Vida helpline for psychological support.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Analysts Raise Mexico's 2026 Growth Forecast</u>

Banxico's October survey of 42 domestic and foreign analysis firms raised Mexico's 2026 GDP forecast from 1.3% to 1.4%, while expected year-end core inflation fell from 4.0% to 3.89% (El Economista). Headline inflation is seen closing 2026 at 3.87%, with the policy rate holding at 6.50% and the peso at 17.50 per dollar.
